children.name: Proseminar Sequence Requirement
children.desc: Complete two proseminar courses, course in the first year of study and an additional course as associated with the student's subplan. course is required for all literature students, course is required for all Chinese linguistics students, and course is required for all Japanese linguistics students. Students in Chinese archaeology must take an advisor-approved course with subject code CHINA, ARCHLGY, or ANTHRO.

children.name: Advisor-Approved Additional Courses Requirement
children.desc: Six advisor-approved courses in Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and/or trans-Asian literature, culture, linguistics, anthropology, archaeology, art and art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, sociology, or another field, as associated with the student's subplan or approved by the advisor, not including courses taken to fulfill the proseminar or language requirements.

Submit a full draft of the student's M.A. thesis to the primary advisor by May 15 of Spring Quarter and the final version by the last Friday of May. Students are also required to present M.A. thesis research at the last meeting of the East Asian Humanities and East Asian Linguistics workshops (the joint student symposium) at the end of Spring Quarter.

children.name: Language Proficiency Requirement
children.desc: Demonstrate proficiency in modern and classical Chinese by completing the following courses or by demonstrating an equivalent level of linguistic attainment by passing the appropriate certifying examinations.

Four advisor-approved courses in Chinese literature, culture, or linguistics from among the offerings of the Department of East Asian Languages and Cultures, not including courses taken to fulfill the language requirement.

Two upper-division or graduate-level courses in fields such as Chinese anthropology, art history, history, philosophy, political science, religious studies, or another field, as approved by the student’s advisor.

children.name: Supporting Language or Laboratory Skill Requirement
children.desc: Demonstrate proficiency in at least one supporting foreign language (in addition to Chinese and English), or in a laboratory skill, to be chosen in consultation with the primary advisor according to the candidate's specific research goals. Proficiency in language(s) and/or laboratory skills must be certified through a written examination or an appropriate amount of course work, to be determined on a case-by-case basis.
